findings.title: b79d54b7 passes the ValidationResult itself to the function, while the spec says the renderer uses its boolean
findings.evidence: The message says 'The check now sees each ValidationResult as its `valid` boolean, the value the spec coerces it to as a DynamicBoolean. The function still receives the result itself.' Spec v1_0 a2ui_protocol.md:1121: 'whenever a DynamicBoolean (such as an argument to and, or, not ...) evaluates to a ValidationResult object ..., the renderer extracts result.valid as its boolean value.'
findings.scenario: A custom function whose DynamicBoolean argument is fed a validation rule receives a ValidationResult rather than the bool the spec promises. Basic and/or/not cope with this, but a custom function might not.
findings.fix: Either say in the message why the result is passed through, or pass the coerced value. This is the core owner's call, so the message at least states the deviation.

votes.reasoning: The divergence is real, but the commit did not introduce it and the message already discloses it. In b79d54b7, `argumentErrors` validates against `checked`, which is `args` passed through `_withValidities`. `invoke` still calls `fn.execute(args, context)` with the original args, so a function whose DynamicBoolean argument is a validation rule receives a ValidationResult. The spec says such functions "receive and return plain booleans", so a custom function written to the spec (for example `args['value'] as bool`) would throw on that argument. That behaviour comes from core's existing design, not from this commit. The basic v1.0 `and`, `or` and `not` read operands through `isTruthyOrValid`, which calls `ValidationResult.validityOf`, so core has always passed the result itself and read its validity inside the function. Before this commit the call failed the schema check outright. The commit makes things strictly better and keeps the existing function contract, which is a defensible minimal choice for a fix in code someone else owns. The message does not mislead: it says the spec coerces the result to its `valid` boolean, then says "The function still receives the result itself." So the minimum fix the finding asks for (state the deviation) is already met. All that is missing is a short reason (the existing catalog functions read the validity themselves through validityOf, and changing what every function receives is the core owner's call). That makes this a nit, not a blocker or misleading-message issue. No probe was needed because the code path is unambiguous.
votes.evidence: Spec specification/v1_0/docs/a2ui_protocol.md, around line 1122: "Functions with `DynamicBoolean` arguments (including `and`, `or`, and `not`) therefore receive and return plain booleans." In dart/a2ui_core/lib/src/resolution/data_context.dart at b79d54b7, `invoke` does `final List<ValidationError> errors = argumentErrors(fn, args); ... return fn.execute(args, context);`, so the original args, not `checked`, reach the function. Pre-existing core design in dart/a2ui_core/lib/src/basic_catalog/function_support.dart:87-88: `bool isTruthyOrValid(Object? value) => ValidationResult.validityOf(value) ?? isTruthy(value);`. Its doc says the v1.0 logic functions use this to read ValidationResult operands, and validation_result.dart:82 `validityOf` handles `ValidationResult(:final valid) => valid`. Commit message b79d54b7: "The check now sees each ValidationResult as its `valid` boolean, the value the spec coerces it to as a DynamicBoolean. The function still receives the result itself."

This is core's pre-existing design (`and`, `or` and `not` read operands through isTruthyOrValid/validityOf), and b79d54b7 keeps it on purpose. The commit message already says the function still receives the result itself, right after saying the spec coerces it. What it lacks is one clause on why: existing functions read the validity themselves, and changing what functions receive is left to the core owner. A one-line addition to the message would close it.

The deviation is real. Spec v1_0 a2ui_protocol.md lines 1121-1122 says the renderer extracts `result.valid` whenever a DynamicBoolean, such as an argument to and/or/not, evaluates to a ValidationResult. It then says "Functions with DynamicBoolean arguments (including and, or, and not) therefore receive and return plain booleans." At b79d54b7, `argumentErrors` passes a coerced copy (`checked`) to the schema check only. `invoke` still calls `fn.execute(args, context)` with the original args, so a custom function gets the ValidationResult object and not the bool.

The finding overstates two things, so I give a corrected claim.
(1) The commit message already states the behaviour: "The function still receives the result itself." It is not hidden. What is missing is any word that this differs from spec line 1122, and why it was kept.
(2) The commit did not introduce the deviation. On base cbaa5ee62, core already relies on functions receiving the result: function_support.dart `isTruthyOrValid` uses `ValidationResult.validityOf`, whose doc says the basic catalog's and/or/not "use it to read their operands". Before this commit, such calls failed the schema check with EXPRESSION_ERROR. After it, built-in functions work and custom functions get the object. That is strictly better, and it matches core's existing design.

Passing the coerced value would change what every core function receives. That is the owner's call and too big for a ride-along fix. It does not coerce a plain map carrying a `valid` key, which `validityOf` does treat as a result. Neither matters for the basic catalog examples.

findings.title: accessibility.hidden on a Modal leaves the open sheet's content, Close button and barrier visible to screen readers
findings.line: 109-110 (ExcludeSemantics in _buildResolved); content built in lib/src/catalog/basic/modal.dart _buildSheet via OverlayPortal
findings.evidence: node_view.dart wraps the node in `ExcludeSemantics(excluding: ComponentProps.asBoolean(read('hidden')) ?? false, ...)`. modal.dart builds `content` through `OverlayPortal(overlayChildBuilder: _buildSheet, ...)`, and the overlay child's render object sits under the Overlay, not under that ExcludeSemantics. Spec v1_0 common_types.json says `hidden` "Hides the element and its children from assistive technologies when true." On web_core the dialog (`role="dialog"` in Modal.ts) is a DOM descendant of the element that gets `aria-hidden`, so it is hidden there. Probe at 3cd032fc: v1.0 surface `{Modal, trigger: btn, content: body, accessibility: {hidden: true}}`; before open the trigger has no semantics node (correct); after tapping 'Open' and pumpAndSettle, walking the semantics tree gives nodes `Dismiss` (barrier), `Dialog`, `Close` and `Secret body`, identical to the hidden=false run.
findings.scenario: An agent hides a decorative or duplicate Modal from assistive technologies. A sighted user opens it, and TalkBack/VoiceOver reads the dialog, its close button and all its content, though the spec says the element's children are hidden. The same happens on a v0.9 surface, since hidden is honoured there too (see the checked items).
findings.fix: In modal.dart, wrap the overlay child in `ExcludeSemantics(excluding: ComponentProps.asBoolean((props.value('accessibility') as Map?)?['hidden']) ?? false, child: ...)`, passing the flag into _Modal. Alternatively list it under the README's known limitations. Add one test that opens a hidden Modal and expects `find.bySemanticsLabel(content text)` to find nothing.

Flutter attaches that overlay child's render object, and so its semantics, under the Overlay, not under the OverlayPortal's ancestors. The ExcludeSemantics therefore covers only the trigger.

The spec text in specification/v1_0/json/common_types.json says `hidden` "Hides the element and its children from assistive technologies when true". Hiding an interactive Modal from assistive technologies is an unusual agent choice, and once the trigger is hidden a screen-reader user cannot reach it alone. It is still a real spec deviation with a one-line fix. One side effect of the fix: it also hides the barrier's BlockSemantics, so the page underneath stays readable while the hidden modal is open. findings.title: accessibility.live on a component whose changing text sits in its own semantics node (Button, CheckBox, TextField) does not announce on Android

findings.title: Slider ignores `steps` above 1000 (moves continuously, writes unsnapped values), and the commit message's reason for the cap is false
findings.evidence: Code: `steps != null && steps >= 1 && steps <= 1000 && range > 0 ? steps.floor() : range > 1 && range <= 1000 && ... ? range.round() : null`, and `final double snapped = divisions == null ? moved : ...`. Commit 3cd032fc says it 'ignores `steps` above 1000, whose tick marks would each be painted'. Flutter's Slider does not paint ticks that are packed too close: flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/material/slider.dart:1830 `if (adjustedTrackWidth / divisions! >= 3.0 * tickMarkWidth) { ...paint ticks }`. My probe confirms it: max 1000 with 1000 divisions and max 100 with 100 divisions draw no ticks at 375 px (screenshot .../probes/shots/feat_slider_dense.png). v1.0 catalog.json Slider.steps: 'If specified, the slider will snap to discrete values.' The schema sets no maximum.
findings.scenario: Probe at 375x812 (.../probes/shots/feat_slider_steps.png and feat_slider_steps.txt): `{max: 2000, steps: 2000}` builds a Slider with `divisions=null`. Dragging writes any double, such as 734.2817, to the bound path, so the snapping the catalog promises does not happen. Slider steps of 5 over 0..10, 4 over 0..1 and 3 over 0..100 render correctly (divisions 5, 4 and 3, with ticks drawn), so only the cap is wrong. The person deciding between port and replace would read a reason in the commit message that is not true.
findings.fix: Snap with the requested count whatever its size: `final int? stepCount = steps != null && steps >= 1 && range > 0 ? steps.floor() : null;`. Use `stepCount` (or the whole-range fallback) for both `divisions` and the snap in onChanged. Flutter already skips the dense ticks. If a guard against absurd values is still wanted, clamp at something like 1 << 31 rather than 1000, or keep `divisions` capped for the widget but snap the written value with `stepCount`. Then correct the 3cd032fc message, which also needs the 'cap them at 1000' subject changed.

votes.reasoning:
Both parts of the finding hold. First, `dart/a2ui_flutter/lib/src/catalog/basic/slider.dart:47-52` only uses `steps` when `steps <= 1000`. For `steps > 1000`, the fallback gives divisions only when the range is a whole number from 2 to 1000, so `{max: 2000, steps: 2000}` gets `divisions = null`. The onChanged handler at lines 85-93 then writes the raw `moved` double, which ignores the catalog's promise that the slider "will snap to discrete values". The schema sets no maximum.

Second, the reason commit 3cd032fc gives for the cap is false. It says it "ignores `steps` above 1000, whose tick marks would each be painted". Flutter's RenderSlider paints ticks only under the guard `if (adjustedTrackWidth / divisions! >= 3.0 * tickMarkWidth)`, with the comment "If the tick marks would be too dense, don't bother painting them". So at any realistic track width, 1000 or more divisions paint no ticks and cost no loop. The other places Flutter uses `divisions` are cheap: discretizing is `(value * divisions).round() / divisions`, and the semantic action unit is `1/divisions`. Nothing there justifies a cap at 1000.

Why should-fix and not blocker: the behaviour gap only appears for `steps > 1000`, which agents rarely send, and nothing crashes. The false rationale does matter, because these commit messages are what the port-or-replace decision rests on, so the message has to change along with the code. Under the brief's strict reading of "misleading commit message", someone could argue for blocker.

One correction to the proposed fix: it drops the cap but must keep a finiteness guard. `double.infinity.floor()` throws `UnsupportedError`, and the old `<= 1000` check was incidentally what blocked that. JSON cannot carry Infinity, but a computed `steps` could. Huge finite values are safe because `floor()` saturates to the int64 maximum. A real but different reason to keep some bound is that with an enormous `divisions` each keyboard or semantic step (`1/divisions`) becomes invisibly small. If the author wants a bound, the message should state that reason instead.

findings.title: In the Markdown fallback, a heading line inside a multi-line Text loses its heading style
findings.scenario: 35_markdown-text at 375 and 800 wide (.../probes/shots/35_markdown-text_375.png): `Heading 1` renders at 14 px regular, identical to the paragraph below it, so the Markdown example's heading is indistinguishable from body text. findings.fix: Build the fallback as `Text.rich` with one span per line: a line matching `_heading` gets `styleOf('h$level')`, and every other line goes through `_withoutMarkers`. That is about six lines and keeps stock widgets. Otherwise leave it as documented.

I could not refute it. In text.dart, `_heading` at line 71 is `RegExp(r'^ {0,3}(#{1,6})[ \t]+([^\n]*?)[ \t#]*$')` without `multiLine: true`. That makes `^` and `$` anchor the whole trimmed string, and `[^\n]*?` cannot cross a newline. So any multi-line Text never matches. It falls through to `_withoutMarkers` (line 77), whose multiLine regex strips the `# ` and leaves the line in body style.

The existing probe dump for the 375 px shot shows the whole block as one Text at 14.0/w400, so the heading line looks the same as the body. The only `A2uiMarkdown(` uses in dart/ are in the README example and markdown_test.dart, so the fallback is the default path.

- The basic_catalog_implementation_guide.md Text guideline only asks the fallback to "attempt to strip common Markdown markers (like `**` or `#`)". The code does that.
- The doc comment (lines 30-32), README L210-212 and CHANGELOG L30-31 all say the heading style applies only when the whole text is one heading line. So no doc misleads.
- The README tells integrators to wrap the surface in an `A2uiMarkdown` for real Markdown rendering.

The proposed per-line `Text.rich` fix would work with stock widgets. It is optional polish, not a bar violation.

findings.title: README Quick Start plus its 'register a catalog of each with one processor' advice sends v0.9 surfaces' messages as v1.0, and drops every outbound message once a v0.9 and a v1.0 surface both send their data model

(1) A v1.0 surface s1 and a v0.9 surface s0, both with sendDataModel true: every sendToAgent call threw 'Multiple protocol versions detected'. Nothing reached the transport: the render-time errors, the Button taps on both surfaces, and any rendererFunctionResponse. The RPC layer drops that response silently, which breaks spec L300's rule that the renderer "MUST always send" a response. A v0.9 agent parsing with RendererToAgentMessagePayload.fromJson(protocolVersion: v0_9) rejects the v1.0 envelope. The v1.0-only Quick Start is correct.

Take the envelope version from the surface: `ErrorMessage(version: surface.protocolVersion!, ...)` in onSurfaceCreated, and `processor.model.getSurface(action.surfaceId)!.protocolVersion!` for actions. In sendToAgent, read `final v = A2uiProtocolVersion.fromJson(message.version)` and send `{v == A2uiProtocolVersion.v0_9 ? findings.title: b79d54b7 coerces only Dart ValidationResult instances, so a ValidationResult object bound from the data model still fails `and`/`or`/`not` with EXPRESSION_ERROR
findings.evidence: `_withValidities` matches only `ValidationResult(:final bool valid) => valid`, and recurses into any other Map. Spec v1.0 L1106: "Validation functions ... or data model bindings evaluate directly to a `ValidationResult` object". L1121: "whenever a `DynamicBoolean` ... evaluates to a `ValidationResult` object (an object with a boolean `valid` property), the renderer extracts `result.valid`". The commit message says "The check now sees each ValidationResult as its `valid` boolean, the value the spec coerces it to as a DynamicBoolean." ValidationResult.validityOf already treats a map with `valid` as one.
findings.scenario: I ran a v1.0 surface with dataModel {check: {valid: true}} and a Button with a check whose condition is `{"@call":"and","args":{"values":[{"@path":"/check"}, true]}}`. The renderer sent {"version":"v1.0","error":{"code":"EXPRESSION_ERROR","surfaceId":"s1","message":"Arguments to 'and' do not match its schema ... at path #root[\"values\"][\"0\"]","details":{"values":[{"valid":true},true]}}}. The Button stayed disabled, and tapping it sent no action. The result is the same before and after b79d54b7.
findings.fix: In `_withValidities`, also map a `Map` whose `valid` is a bool to that bool, for example `final Map<String, Object?> map when map['valid'] is bool => map['valid']` before the recursive Map case. If object-typed parameters must keep such maps, restrict this to parameters whose resolved schema is boolean. Add a core test with a path-bound operand.

votes.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. Spec v1.0 lines 1106 and 1121 say a data model binding can evaluate to a ValidationResult object. When a DynamicBoolean such as an `and`/`or`/`not` argument does, the spec says the renderer extracts `result.valid`. The functions themselves already handle a `{valid}` map, because `truthy` uses `ValidationResult.validityOf`, which accepts any Map with a `valid` key. The schema check in `Catalog.invoke` runs first, though. b79d54b7's `_withValidities` replaces only Dart `ValidationResult` instances and passes a plain map `{valid: true}` through unchanged. That map then fails the resolved DynamicBoolean `oneOf` (boolean | DataBinding `{@path}` | FunctionCall), so invoke throws EXPRESSION_ERROR before the function runs.

This is not a regression from the branch. It fails the same way on the base. It is a gap in a fix whose commit message says it applies the spec's DynamicBoolean coercion, while the fix covers only results returned by functions. The same gap hits a ValidationResult-shaped map from any other source, for example a nested call result that was serialised. It is not a blocker. The motivating examples (09, 32) use function-returned results, which the commit does fix, and a binding to a stored `{valid}` object is a less common pattern. It is still a real spec deviation in a core fix that claims spec coercion, and the fix is one line, so should-fix is right.

The proposed fix works as stated. With it applied, the full core suite passes and both probes return true. One caveat: it rewrites any map with a bool `valid` at any depth, including inside object-typed parameters. No current basic-catalog function seems affected (the suite is green). Limiting the rewrite to DynamicBoolean positions would be stricter, but probably goes beyond what a viable fix needs.

votes.corrected_claim: b79d54b7 does not edit rpc_handler.dart. It changes the shared `argumentErrors`, so the agent RPC path (rpc_handler.dart:393) now also accepts ValidationResult arguments and runs the function. The commit message and the CHANGELOG name only Catalog.invoke, and no RPC test covers this. On both paths the function still receives the ValidationResult itself rather than the boolean that spec rule 1 (line 1122) calls for. The message says this but gives no reason. findings.title: A callRendererFunction without catalogId makes processMessages throw, and the README's onAgentMessages only logs it, so the agent gets neither a rendererFunctionResponse nor an error
findings.evidence: README L38-39: "Actions, errors and the processor's function calls and answers go back to the agent." L77-78 catch the A2uiError and only `log(...)` it. Spec v1.0 L309: if catalogId is "omitted or unregistered, the renderer rejects the call with `code: \"INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL\"`". L1494-1501: envelope-level function invocation faults are sent as an `error` naming the `functionCallId`.
findings.scenario: The agent sends {"version":"v1.0","callRendererFunction":{"surfaceId":"s1","functionCallId":"c7","callFunction":{"@call":"echoFlag","args":{"flag":true}}}}. processMessagesAsync throws 'missing required field catalogId', and no message reaches the agent, which waits on c7 until it times out. This is core behaviour that predates the branch, but the rewritten Quick Start now says errors go back to the agent.
findings.fix: Narrow the README sentence to say surface actions, surface errors and RPC answers go back. Or, in the catch, send an `ErrorMessage` for a rejected callRendererFunction that names its functionCallId. A core change that answers with INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL belongs to the core owners.

votes.reasoning: The behaviour is real. AgentToRendererMessage.fromJson (dart/a2ui_core/lib/src/core/messages.dart L138-149, _callFunction L527-535) requires callFunction.catalogId for callRendererFunction and throws A2uiValidationError while parsing. Every message in processMessages and processMessagesAsync is parsed through _route before anything is applied (processor.dart L317-345), so the throw escapes before RpcHandler.handleCallRendererFunction runs. That handler is the only path that turns faults into a rendererFunctionResponse. The README Quick Start (L74-80) catches A2uiError and only logs it, so the agent gets neither a rendererFunctionResponse nor an `error` naming functionCallId. That breaks spec v1.0 L309 ("rejects the call with INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL") and L1494-1501, which route envelope-level invocation faults through `error` with functionCallId. A probe confirmed the throw and that nothing goes out. One correction to the claim: the error code is VALIDATION_FAILED, not INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL. The gap also covers any malformed envelope, not only a missing catalogId. The core gap predates the branch and belongs to the a2ui_core owners. The branch's own part is the rewritten README sentence at L38-39, "Actions, errors and the processor's function calls and answers go back to the agent", which overstates what the snippet does. Read in context, "errors" plausibly means the surface onError errors the snippet wires up, so it is a nit, not should-fix. Smallest fix: narrow the sentence to surface actions, surface errors and RPC answers, or say that a payload processMessages rejects is only logged in this sketch.
votes.evidence: Probe run in a throwaway worktree at HEAD 3cd032fc (dart/a2ui_core): a MessageProcessor<ComponentApi>(catalogs: [BasicCatalog.v1_0()], outboundListener: collect) was given processMessagesAsync({"version":"v1.0","callRendererFunction":{"functionCallId":"c7","callFunction":{"@call":"formatString","args":{"value":"x"}}}}). Output: `ERR: A2uiValidationError [VALIDATION_FAILED]: Message 'callRendererFunction.callFunction' is missing required field 'catalogId'.` and `OUT: []` (the outbound listener got nothing). Code: messages.dart L148 `callFunction: _callFunction(body, key, requireCatalogId: true)` and L533-534 `if (requireCatalogId) { _required<String>(call, 'catalogId', type); }`. processor.dart L318-320 parses every item via _route before applying any. README L77-79 `} on A2uiError catch (error) { log('${error.code}: ${error.message}'); }`. Spec L309: "if omitted or unregistered, the renderer rejects the call with `code: \"INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL\"`". Spec L1491 and L1500: the `error` message carries functionCallId for envelope-level function invocation faults. The worktree was removed afterwards.
votes.corrected_claim: The claim is correct, with two refinements. The thrown error is A2uiValidationError with code VALIDATION_FAILED, not INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL. And any envelope that processMessages rejects while parsing is likewise only logged by the README snippet. The branch-attributable defect is only the overbroad README sentence at L38-39. The missing INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL reply is a core gap that predates the branch.

votes.reasoning:
I couldn't refute the finding. The core parser requires catalogId on a callRendererFunction. A call without one throws A2uiValidationError while the payload is being routed, before any rpc work starts. So no rendererFunctionResponse goes out, and the README's onAgentMessages only logs the error. The spec says such a call is rejected with INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL and that envelope-level function faults go back as an `error` naming the functionCallId, so the agent is never told.

The root cause is core behaviour that this branch did not introduce. The pre-branch README already only logged processMessages errors. What the branch changed is the Quick Start sentence: it went from "Actions and errors on a surface go back to the agent" to "Actions, errors and the processor's function calls and answers go back to the agent". Dropping "on a surface" makes the doc promise more than the sample does. Payload-level errors still only reach a log: a malformed envelope, an unknown surface, or a callRendererFunction without catalogId.

This is a small doc overclaim in sample code, not a renderer bug, so it is a nit. The smallest fix is to put the scope back, for example "Actions and errors on a surface, and the processor's function calls and answers, go back to the agent". The option of sending an ErrorMessage from the catch is extra. A core fix belongs to the core owners.
votes.evidence:
- README diff at L38-39: "-...Actions and errors on\n-a surface go back to the agent." became "+...Actions, errors and\n+the processor's function calls and answers go back to the agent." The README at L74-80 is unchanged in substance: `} on A2uiError catch (error) { log('${error.code}: ${error.message}'); }`.
- dart/a2ui_core/lib/src/core/messages.dart:138-148: the callRendererFunction case calls `_callFunction(body, key, requireCatalogId: true)`. At L536-538, `if (requireCatalogId) { _required<String>(call, 'catalogId', type); }` throws a validation error when the field is missing.
- processor.dart:316-318: processMessages routes every item (`_route(item)`) before it applies any, so the parse error escapes before `_callRendererFunction` or rpc runs. The comment "handleCallRendererFunction answers errors instead" covers only calls that parsed.
- Spec v1_0 a2ui_protocol.md L309: "if omitted or unregistered, the renderer rejects the call with `code: \"INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL\"`". The `error` message section (around L1494-1501) defines `functionCallId` for "function invocation errors outside a `rendererFunctionResponse`".
- I ran no probe. Reading the code settles the throw path: _required throws, and routing happens before apply.
votes.corrected_claim: This is mostly accurate as stated. More precisely: a callRendererFunction without catalogId fails while the payload is parsed and routed, so neither processMessages nor processMessagesAsync gets to the rpc layer. The same log-only handling applies to every payload-level error, such as a malformed envelope or an unknown surface, and the pre-branch README had it too. The branch's own fault is the rewritten sentence, which dropped the "on a surface" scope and now overclaims.
